questions.question_english: A student who attributes their success to internal, stable, and controllable factors is exhibiting a motivational profile that leads to:
options_english: Learned helplessness
High resilience and persistence
Extreme anxiety and fear of failure
Complete dependence on the teacher
questions.explanation_english: In Bernard Weiner's Attribution Theory of motivation, causal attributions for academic outcomes govern emotional reactions and future achievement expectations. Attributing success to internal factors (ability, dedication), stable factors (consistent effort and sustained knowledge), and controllable factors (deliberate practice, strategic planning) produces feelings of pride, self-competence, and high self-efficacy. Because learners perceive that their own efforts directly determine outcomes and can be replicated in future tasks, they demonstrate remarkable academic resilience, bounce back from setbacks, and exhibit sustained persistence.
questions.explanation_hindi: बर्नार्ड वेनर (Bernard Weiner) के गुणारोपण सिद्धांत के अनुसार, जब कोई विद्यार्थी अपनी सफलता को आंतरिक (स्वयं की क्षमता), स्थिर (निरंतर अभ्यास), और नियंत्रणीय (सुनियोजित प्रयास व रणनीति) कारकों से जोड़ता है, तो उसमें उच्च आत्म-प्रभावोत्पादकता (self-efficacy) का विकास होता है। वह यह समझता है कि उसकी सफलता भाग्य या शिक्षक की कृपा पर नहीं, बल्कि उसके अपने प्रयासों पर निर्भर करती है। यह विश्वास उसे चुनौतियों का सामना करने की प्रेरणा, विफलता से उबरने का उच्च लचीलापन (resilience) और कठिन परिस्थितियों में भी दृढ़ता प्रदान करता है। अतः विकल्प (B) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) High resilience and persistence

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Attributing success to internal, stable, and controllable factors builds high self-efficacy and resilience, as students recognize that sustained competence and effort directly produce successful outcomes.

questions.question_english: The ‘Index for Inclusion’, developed by Tony Booth and Mel Ainscow, is an internationally acclaimed self-evaluation resource that assists schools to:
options_english: Systematically rank enrolled students with disabilities based on formal clinical intelligence quotient (IQ) assessment scores
Identify and remove learning barriers through inclusive culture, policy, and practice reforms
Calculate annual financial capital expenditure required to establish and maintain specialized segregated institutional facilities
Segregate diverse student cohorts into separate physical classrooms based upon primary native language spoken at home
questions.explanation_english:
The ‘Index for Inclusion: Developing Learning and Participation in Schools’, created by Tony Booth and Mel Ainscow and published by the Centre for Studies on Inclusive Education (CSIE), is a globally celebrated school self-review and development tool.
- Core Purpose: It guides school principals, teachers, students, parents, and community stakeholders through a collaborative cycle of internal reflection to identify and eliminate systemic barriers to learning and participation.
- Three Interrelated Dimensions: The Index structures school transformation around three foundational pillars:
  1. Creating inclusive CULTURES (establishing deeply shared inclusive values and collaborative communities);
  2. Producing inclusive POLICIES (designing school organization and support structures for all learners);
  3. Evolving inclusive PRACTICES (adapting classroom teaching and mobilizing community resources).
By moving the analytical focus away from 'fixing the deficit within the child' toward reforming institutional barriers in cultures, policies, and practices, the Index embodies genuine educational inclusion. Therefore, Option B is correct.
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Identify and remove learning barriers through inclusive culture and policy reforms

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: through inclusive culture and policy reforms The ‘Index for Inclusion’, developed by Tony Booth and Mel Ainscow, is a comprehensive self-evaluation framework used worldwide. It assists school communities in systematically reviewing and improving school cultures, policies, and classroom practices, helping identify and eliminate learning barriers to foster inclusion for all students.

questions.question_english: Article 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) explicitly and unconditionally prohibits which of the following acts?
options_english: Arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile of individuals
Arbitrary interference with personal privacy, family, or correspondence
Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment
Subjection to slavery, servitude, or the transatlantic slave trade
questions.explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment.

Detailed Justification and Legal Analysis:
1. Text of Article 5: Article 5 of the UDHR states in absolute terms: 'No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.'
2. Non-Derogable and Absolute Character: The prohibition against torture is an absolute, non-derogable human right (jus cogens). It cannot be suspended under any circumstances—even during states of war, public emergency, or anti-terror operations. This principle is codified in the UN Convention Against Torture (UNCAT, 1984) and Article 7 of the ICCPR.
3. Indian Jurisprudence: Although India has not yet enacted a specific standalone anti-torture statute, the Supreme Court of India in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997) held that custodial torture, rape, or death violates Article 21 of the Constitution and constitutes a direct assault on human dignity under Article 5 of the UDHR.
4. Mapping of Other Articles:
   - Article 4 prohibits slavery and servitude.
   - Article 9 prohibits arbitrary arrest, detention, or exile.
   - Article 12 prohibits arbitrary interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) यातना अथवा क्रूर, अमानवीय या अपमानजनक व्यवहार या दंड।

विस्तृत व्याख्या एवं विधिक विश्लेषण:
1. UDHR के अनुच्छेद 5 का मूल पाठ: 'किसी भी व्यक्ति को यातना अथवा क्रूर, अमानवीय या अपमानजनक व्यवहार या दंड के अधीन नहीं किया जाएगा' (No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment)।
2. अनुलंघनीय अधिकार (Non-Derogable Right): यातना का प्रतिषेध अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विधि में एक पूर्ण एवं अहस्तांतरणीय सिद्धांत (Jus Cogens) है। युद्ध, आपातकाल या राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा जैसी किसी भी परिस्थिति में इसका उल्लंघन नहीं किया जा सकता। संयुक्त राष्ट्र का यातना-विरोधी अभिसमय (UNCAT, 1984) इसी सिद्धांत को संहिताबद्ध करता है।
3. भारतीय न्यायशास्त्र: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने डी.के. बसु बनाम पश्चिम बंगाल राज्य (1997) मामले में ऐतिहासिक निर्णय देते हुए गिरफ्तारी और हिरासत के संबंध में सख्त दिशानिर्देश तय किए तथा स्पष्ट किया कि पुलिस हिरासत में यातना संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 और UDHR के अनुच्छेद 5 का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
4. अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 4 दासता पर रोक लगाता है; अनुच्छेद 9 मनमानी गिरफ्तारी व निर्वासन का प्रतिषेध करता है; और अनुच्छेद 12 निजता के अधिकार की रक्षा करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights establishes an absolute, non-derogable prohibition against cruel treatment. It explicitly mandates that no individual shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment under any circumstances, ensuring complete protection of bodily integrity and human dignity across all jurisdictions globally.
